question: A 3175-g (7-lb) female newborn is delivered at term. Initial examination shows a distended abdomen and a flat perineal region without an opening. A dark green discharge is coming out of the vulva. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Distended abdomen and flat perineal region without an opening" -> "Dark green discharge from vulva" -> "Imperforate anus" -> 95% CHAIN: "Distended abdomen and flat perineal region without an opening" -> "Dark green discharge from vulva" -> "Meconium ileus" -> 90% CHAIN: "Distended abdomen and flat perineal region without an opening" -> "Dark green discharge from vulva" -> "Hirschsprung disease" -> 70% CHAIN: "Distended abdomen and flat perineal region without an opening" -> "Dark green discharge from vulva" -> "Colonic atresia" -> 60% CHAIN: "Distended abdomen and flat perineal region without an opening" -> "Dark green discharge from vulva" -> "Meconium plug syndrome" -> 95%
enhanced_information: The most likely diagnosis for the newborn with a distended abdomen, flat perineal region without an opening, and dark green discharge from the vulva is Imperforate anus. This is supported by the presence of a dark green discharge from the vulva, which can be associated with an imperforate anus. Hirschsprung disease and other options are less likely based on the clinical presentation.
analysis: The core medical principle in this case is to recognize the clinical presentation of a distended abdomen, flat perineal region without an opening, and dark green discharge from the vulva in a newborn. Imperforate anus is the most likely diagnosis based on this presentation. Meconium ileus, Hirschsprung disease, colonic atresia, and meconium plug syndrome are less likely given the specific findings described.
